Characterise nucleotide composition of DNA sequences

Source: R/parse.R
rb_sequence_composition.Rd

Reports the character-class composition of sequences without modifying them. Separates unambiguous bases, IUPAC ambiguity codes, gap characters and any other characters, so that quality control can distinguish formatting artefacts from genuine base-calling uncertainty.

Usage

rb_sequence_composition(sequence)

Arguments

sequence

Character vector of nucleotide sequences. Case is ignored. NA values are treated as empty strings.

Value

A data.frame with one row per input sequence:

n_char

Total characters in the stored string.

n_acgt

Count of unambiguous bases (A, C, G, T).

n_dash

Count of hyphen (-) characters.

n_dot

Count of period (.) characters.

n_ambig

Count of IUPAC ambiguity codes (R, Y, K, M, S, W, B, D, H, V, N).

n_other

Count of characters belonging to none of the above classes.

n_gap_runs

Number of contiguous runs of gap characters.

max_gap_run

Length of the longest contiguous gap run; 0 if none.

n_base

Biological length, n_acgt + n_ambig. Excludes gap characters.

frac_ambig

n_ambig / n_base; NA when n_base is 0.

Details

Gap characters are not stripped or altered. Their meaning is context-dependent: they may be alignment padding, a genuine deletion relative to other sequences in an alignment, or undetermined bases in the source record. These cases cannot be distinguished from the character alone, so they are reported separately and any normalisation is left to an explicit, user-initiated step.

IUPAC codes are retained as information. Use n_base as the denominator for ambiguity fractions and as the length measure for marker-level checks; n_char reflects the stored string and may be inflated by padding.

See also

Other parsing: rb_ambiguity_utils, rb_combine_resolve, rb_parse_sources, rb_sequence_prep

Examples

x <- rb_sequence_composition(c("ACGTACGT", "ACGT-ACGT", "ACGTNACGT", "ACGT..ACGT"))
x$n_char   # 8  9  9 10  (stored string)
#> [1]  8  9  9 10
x$n_base   # 8  8  9  8  (biological length)
#> [1] 8 8 9 8
